analysis.title: Rates Spark: Don't expect a break back below 5%
key_insights: ING expects the US 10-year Treasury yield to stay above 5.00% and head back up to 5.25%. It would be quite surprised by a break below 5%.

Treasury buyers appeared around 5.3% after the Wednesday CPI release, and Asian-open equity falls, especially in Korea, prompted follow-on buying. Steady dip buying in recent weeks had not produced a meaningful drop in yields because it was offset by net shorts in Treasury futures.
Thursday's data (low jobless claims, firm retail sales, uncomfortably high PPI) did not move Treasuries. ING expects the market to use it as a platform to rebuild higher yields into the mid-terms.
Neither political side has voiced an intention to act on the fiscal deficit. High printed inflation and a high deficit remain the issues.
ING sees at least one more leg of long-end weakness, taking the US 10-year into a 5.25% to 5.5% range. Other markets would move in tandem with less dramatic blow-outs.
ING sees 5.25% as a mean-reversion level. The 10-year could overshoot toward 5.5% and stay elevated for months, possibly into Q1 2027. Its views are unchanged despite recent moves.

In the eurozone, France is setting the mood. The French 10-year swap spread has doubled from about 60bp to about 120bp, and French spreads to Germany are about as wide as at any point since the start of the euro.

ING says the French widening is probably overdone. A swing to the right could bring tail positives that are not discounted. Italian spreads have improved gradually under Meloni and have been low beta to French concerns.
The first real bout of French spread widening traces to Macron's mid-2024 election gamble. The recent spike amplifies an underlying tension that never went away.
ING says bonds generally remain in a danger zone and more upside overshoots in yields are foreseeable in both the US and France.

tension_points.bear_case: Strong data, high PPI, a large deficit and net futures shorts point to a rebuild of yields toward 5.25% to 5.5% into the mid-terms.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A break below 5% on the US 10-year yield would surprise ING and challenge its view.

tension_points.bear_case: French debt dynamics, a lack of ambition to correct them and the political options for 2028 keep spreads wide, and more overshoots are foreseeable.
